questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to become a beekeeper
Why honey is good for your health
Whether eating honey can help bees, and the problems wild bees face
Why vegans don't eat honey
questions.why: They discuss a listener's question, 'Can honey help save bees?', and the decline of wild bees.

questions.q: What does Phil say about honey?
options: He uses it a lot when he cooks
He never eats it
He keeps his own bees so he can make honey
He only eats it when he is ill
questions.why: Phil says he uses honey a lot in cooking.

questions.q: Why was honey called 'liquid gold' in ancient times?
options: Because it was used to make coins
Because only kings and queens were allowed to eat it at their feasts
Because bees were very rare
Because people valued its taste and its use as medicine
questions.why: Beth says honey was prized for its taste and medicinal properties.

questions.q: What is listener Saoirse unsure about?
options: Whether she should stop being vegan and start eating honey again
Whether eating honey might help declining bee populations
Whether honey is safe for children
Whether honey bees are dangerous
questions.why: She doesn't eat honey but asks 'can honey help save bees?' because bee populations are declining.

questions.q: What do we learn about honey bees?
options: They are one of the most endangered insects in the whole world
They are very widespread and not endangered
There are only 26 species left
They only live in the UK
questions.why: Phil says honey bees are one of the most widespread insects and 'not endangered at all'.

questions.q: What does biologist Dave Goulson say about bumblebees in the UK?
options: All 26 species are doing well across the country
Numbers are rising quickly
They live mainly in cities
Three of the 26 species have died out
questions.why: He says the UK has 26 bumblebee species, but three have gone extinct.

questions.q: Why does Dave Goulson mention beekeepers?
options: To explain why wild bees are more at risk than honey bees
To say that beekeepers are harming wild bees by keeping too many hives
To suggest everyone should keep bees
To show how much money honey makes
questions.why: He says honey bees have beekeepers, 'but nobody's looking out for the wild bees'.

questions.q: What does Phil suggest people can do to help wild bees?
options: Eat more honey
Buy honey only from small local farms near where they live
Grow plants that bees like, such as lavender
Stop using cow manure on gardens
questions.why: He says eating more honey won't do much, but you can grow bee-friendly plants like lavender.
